title: The sleeping brain's rhythm-within-a-rhythm: slow-oscillation<->spindle coupling, validated against tensorpac

dataset.name: Sleep-EDF Expanded (sleep-edfx)
dataset.record: subject SC4001, overnight PSG; EEG Fpz-Cz at 100 Hz; the first 30 min of concatenated NREM (N2+N3) epochs from the expert hypnogram
dataset.citation: Kemp B, Zwinderman AH, Tuk B, Kamphuisen HAC, Oberye JJL. Analysis of a sleep-dependent neuronal feedback loop: the slow-wave microcontinuity of the EEG. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2000;47(9):1185-1194. Sleep-EDF Expanded, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).

proposition: During deep sleep the brain nests one rhythm inside another: the up-state of the slow oscillation (~1 Hz) gates the thalamocortical sleep spindles (~13 Hz), so the spindle amplitude rises and falls with the slow-oscillation phase. This slow-oscillation<->spindle coupling is a hallmark of NREM sleep and is implicated in memory consolidation. Measuring it on a real overnight polysomnogram with the Tort modulation index gives MI = 0.00035 on the NREM EEG (Fpz-Cz), and it is unmistakably real: the observed coupling sits z = 9.6 above a circular-shift surrogate null and exceeds every one of 200 surrogates. The ecosystem's phaseAmplitudeCoupling reproduces the canonical Python tensorpac to machine precision (|difference| = 5e-17) -- fed the identical phase and amplitude, the two engines return the same modulation index to the last digit. The coupling is a genuine physiological signal, and the operator that finds it is exactly the field-standard one.

claims.statement: SO-spindle Tort modulation index on the NREM EEG (SO phase 0.5-1.25 Hz, spindle amp 12-15 Hz)
the same Tort MI recomputed by the canonical Python tensorpac (op == tensorpac)
z-score of the observed MI against a circular-shift surrogate null (real coupling)
surrogates (of 200) the observed MI exceeds -- significance of the coupling

validation.reference: tensorpac (Python; Combrisson et al. 2020) is a canonical reference implementation of phase-amplitude coupling, and the Tort modulation index (Tort et al. 2010) is a standard PAC statistic. A correct implementation must reproduce it. Fed the IDENTICAL phase + amplitude, phaseAmplitudeCoupling and tensorpac.methods.modulation_index return the same Tort MI to machine precision (|diff| = 5e-17) on the real NREM EEG. The coupling is shown genuine by a circular-shift surrogate null: the observed MI is z = 9.6 above the surrogate mean and exceeds all 200 surrogates.
validation.data: REAL -- Sleep-EDF Expanded (sleep-edfx, PhysioNet), subject SC4001 overnight PSG, EEG Fpz-Cz, 30 min of NREM (N2+N3)
validation.note: The reproducible findings are (1) the SO-spindle coupling is real -- observed MI z = 9.6 above a circular-shift null, exceeding all 200 surrogates -- and (2) phaseAmplitudeCoupling == tensorpac to machine precision. HONEST scope: (1) the two engines are fed the IDENTICAL phase + amplitude (the same .pac_extract feeds both), so the machine-precision agreement validates the Tort-MI computation, not the whole filtering chain; (2) significance is established against a circular-shift surrogate null (a standard, conservative PAC control), not merely by a non-zero MI; (3) single subject, single channel (Fpz-Cz), first 30 min of NREM -- the absolute MI magnitude depends on the montage and the chosen SO/spindle bands, so it is a demonstration of the method + a real coupling, not a normative value; (4) run_simulation = FALSE -- the op is deterministic and the surrogate null is seeded, so the reported z replays.

open_questions.q: The coupling was measured on one channel of one night. Its preferred SO phase (where spindles peak) and its strength are themselves biomarkers: tracking them across N2 vs N3, across the night, across subjects, and against a memory-task outcome would turn this validated PAC operator into a sleep/memory study; a comodulogram (a grid of phase x amplitude bands) would locate the coupling in frequency space rather than assuming the SO/spindle bands. Documented, not escalated.
